subject: Trading
title: Currency Correlations
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Currency Correlations.

hook.text: EUR/USD and GBP/USD often move together. USD/CHF moves opposite. Knowing this prevents accidental doubling up.

buildup.text: Correlation measures how two pairs move relative to each other, from +1 (identical) to -1 (opposite).

discovery.text: AUD/USD and NZD/USD are highly correlated—both commodity currencies driven by Asian demand.

twist.text: Correlations break during crises. Pairs that normally move together can suddenly diverge violently.

climax.text: Traders use correlations to diversify or hedge—but must remember that correlations aren't constants.

punchline.text: Correlated pairs double your bet, not your edge.

quiz.question: Why should forex traders watch currency correlations?
options: To avoid accidentally doubling exposure to the same move
